rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who settled the abode and faith” refers to the Ansar.
rows.anchor: Ve şunlar ki bunlardan murad ensardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers connecting the Ansar to the Muhajirun; this gives them a share in fayʾ like the Muhajirun.
rows.anchor: Birincisi “muhâcirîn” üzerine ma‘tuf olmasıdır ki en râcih olan da budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis connects them to فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ, making their participation in sincerity explicit and their share in fayʾ implicit.
rows.anchor: Bu surette onlara sadakatte iştirakleri tasrih edilmiş, fey’e iştirak hakları delâleten anlatılmış olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis takes the waw as introductory, with الذين as subject and يحبون as predicate; their virtues are stated independently, while fayʾ entitlement remains implicit.
rows.anchor: Üçüncüsü ma‘tuf olmayıp vav istînâfiye, وَٱلَّذِينَ mübtedâ, يُحِبُّونَ haber olmaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In any syntactic analysis, praising altruism presupposes a right or entitlement to relinquish; preference has no sense where there is no right to give up.
rows.anchor: Çünkü üç takdirde de îsâr ile medih, esas itibariyle bir istihkak veya salâhiyetin sübûtunu ifade eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabawwaʾ can mean preparing or being prepared, as well as taking a place or abode.
rows.anchor: تبوئه وتبوء gibi hazırlamak ve hazırlanmak mânalarına geldiği gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb can also mean lodging in a place, marrying, or taking a place as one's abode.
rows.anchor: bir mekâna, bir konağa konmak, tezevvüc etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dār denotes a bounded, fully equipped dwelling or homeland; here it means the abode of Islam, indicated by the mention of faith.
rows.anchor: Burada “ed-dâr”dan murad da iman karînesiyle dâr-ı İslâm’dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes identify the first abode of Islam as Medina, where Muslims first lived and Islamic civilization began to develop.
rows.anchor: ilk dâr-ı İslâm, ehl-i İslâm’ın ilk barındığı ve İslâm medeniyetinin ilk inkişâfa başladığı Medîne-i Münevvere olduğundan müfessirîn bunu Medine diye tefsir etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats al-īmān as a comitative object coordinated with al-dār; this avoids supplying an omitted verb such as “they sincerely embraced faith.”
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye’nin dediği gibi mef‘ûl-i ma‘ah olması da güzel bir vecihtir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some Muhajirun believed earlier, the Ansar preceded them in preparing Medina as an abode through faith, so they are called the ones who came before.
rows.anchor: iman ile Medine’yi ihzar etmek itibariyle ensar mukaddem olduğu cihetle مِن قَبْلِهِمْ buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min qablihim may mean before the migrants' arrival; īmān may also derive from the causative of safety, describing the Ansar securing Medina as an Islamic abode by the Aqaba pledge.
rows.anchor: burada مِن قَبْلِهِمْ onların hicretlerinden evvel demek olabileceği gibi; “îmân”, “emn” ü “emân”dan if‘âl olmak da melhuzdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the Ansar secured Medina as an abode of Islam before the migration through the Aqaba pledge.
rows.anchor: ensar, muhâcirînin hicretinden evvel Akabe Bey’atı’yla vatanları olan Medine’yi dâr-ı İslâm yapmak üzere te’mîn edip imana sâhip oldular.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ansar loved those who migrated to them, beginning with the Prophet, whether the migrants were rich or poor; this displayed their sincerity.
rows.anchor: başta Peygamber olmak üzere hicret eden o sâdıkları gerek zengin

words: وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِى صُدُورِهِمْ حَاجَةًۭ مِّمَّآ أُوتُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They felt no inward regret about what was given to the migrants from fayʾ or other resources, as though it had been something they themselves needed.
rows.anchor: yani muhacirlere gerek fey’ ve gerek sâireden verilen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of īthār is omitted; it may be the migrants or, more broadly, fellow believers whose needs the Ansar put ahead of their own.
rows.anchor: Burada “îsâr”ın mef‘ûlü hazfedilmiştir. Binâen‘aleyh muhâcirîn yahut da e‘am olmak muhtemildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They gave others' needs precedence over their own, even when they themselves lacked necessities; the author calls this the highest generosity and selflessness.
rows.anchor: daha üstün tutarak onları nefislerine takdim ve tercih ederler

rows.speaker: Müfessirînin bir kısmı
rows.claim: A report about the distribution of Banu Nadir property says the Prophet allocated it to the Muhajirun, apart from three needy Ansar; the Ansar then offered their own wealth and homes and declined a share in that booty. Some exegetes call this the occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînin bir kısmı sebeb-i nüzûlün bu olduğunu söylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that an Ansari, identified as Abu Talha in one version, hosted a starving man; the couple put their child to sleep, extinguished the lamp, and went hungry, after which the Prophet said God was pleased with them and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: Buhârî, Müslim, Tirmizî, Nesâî ve daha bazıları Ebû Hüreyre’den şöyle rivayet etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that a sheep's head passed among seven households as each preferred a brother and his family, then returned to the first home; the verse was revealed about this.
rows.anchor: Hâkim ve İbn Merdûye ve Şu‘ab’da Beyhakī dahi İbn Ömer radıyallâhu anhümâ Hazretleri’nden şöyle rivayet etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited occasions are only examples; the Ansar and Companions displayed many such acts, including men with two wives giving one up so an unmarried Muhajir could marry.
rows.anchor: Hatta ensardan iki zevcesi bulunanlar zevcesi olmayan muhacirlerin evlenmesi için zevcelerinden birini terk bile etmişlerdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Yarmuk, dying wounded martyrs passed even a sip of water to a groaning companion; Akif's Safahat beautifully depicts the sacred historical episode.
rows.anchor: Yermük vak‘asında şehidler içinde son nefesine gelmiş yaralıların kendilerine verilen bir yudum suyu bile yanında inleyen arkadaşına

words: وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِۦ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those protected from the soul's shuhh—greed, envy, and stinginess—are the truly successful, escaping every harm and attaining their aims; this is both an ethical principle and glad tidings for the Ansar and their imitators.
rows.anchor: ahlâkī bir saadet düstûru, hem de ensârın ve onların ahlâklarına imtisal edenlerin medhiyle haklarında bir tebşirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuhh is an ingrained disposition of greed, envy, and miserliness; buhl is its practical manifestation in withholding.
rows.anchor: “Şuhh” nefsin bahillik, nekeslik, hasislik dediğimiz hırs ve kıskançlık huyudur

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib defines shuhh as greed and miserliness that have become habitual.
rows.anchor: Râgıb bunu “âdet hâline gelmiş hırs ile buhl” diye târif etmiştir.

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Hasan distinguishes buhl as begrudging what one owns from shuhh as begrudging what anyone else owns.
rows.anchor: İbn Münzir’in Hasan’dan rivayetine göre “buhl” insanın elindekini kıskanması, “şuhh” da herkesin elindekini kıskanması diye târif edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: Ibn Masud tells a man who fears his stinginess means doom that this is buhl, not Quranic shuhh; shuhh is unjustly consuming one's brother's property.
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd Hazretleri de “o şuhh değil, buhldur, buhlde de hayır yoktur. Allah teâlâ’nın zikrettiği şuhh ise kardeşinin malını zulmen yemendir” diye cevap vermiştir.

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says shuhh is not withholding one's own property but coveting what does not belong to oneself.
rows.anchor: İbn Münzir’in ve İbn Merdûye’nin rivayet ettikleri vechile İbn Ömer radıyallâhu anhümâ Hazretleri de demiştir ki

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi finds no lexicographers' support for those definitions and suggests shuhh is buhl at its extreme: resenting others' generosity, trying to stop it, wrongfully taking their property, or envying what they have.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî bunları naklettikten sonra der ki: “Lügaviyyûnun hiçbirinde ‘şuhh’un bu târiflerinden bir şey görmedim

words: وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِۦ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns shuhh as extremely blameworthy: success is restricted to those protected from it, excluding those who are not protected.
rows.anchor: şuhdan vikāye edilenlere kasredilmiş olmakla ondan vikāye edilmemiş olanlar felah bulanların hâricinde kalmış olur.

rows.speaker: Enes
rows.claim: A Prophetic report from Anas says nothing destroys Islam as completely as shuhh.
rows.anchor: Hakîm-i Tirmizî ve Ebû Ya‘lâ ve İbn Merdûye Enes radıyallâhu anh’tan merfû‘an rivayet etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
rows.claim: A Prophetic report from Abu Hurayra says the dust of God's path and Hell's smoke never coexist in a servant's body, nor faith and shuhh in a heart.
rows.anchor: İbn Ebî Şeybe, Nesâî ve Beyhakī ve Hâkim Ebû Hüreyre radıyallâhu anh’tan merfû‘an rivayet etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: Ebû Sa‘îd-i Hudrî
rows.claim: A Prophetic report from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri says stinginess and bad character do not coexist in a Muslim; Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb.
rows.anchor: Ebû Dâvûd, Tirmizî “garîb” diyerek, Edeb’de Buhârî ve daha diğerleri Ebû Sa‘îd-i Hudrî radıyallâhu anh’tan merfû‘an rivayet eylemişlerdir

words: وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِۦ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ
rows.speaker: Enes
rows.claim: In a report from Anas, God commands Eden to speak; it says “The believers have succeeded,” and God swears no miser will dwell near Him there. The Prophet then recites 59:9.
rows.anchor: İbn Ebi’d- Dünya ve İbn Adî ve Hâkim ve Hatîb Enes radıyallâhu anh’tan rivayet etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: Câbir b. Abdillah
rows.claim: A Prophetic report from Jabir warns against injustice and shuhh: shuhh destroyed earlier peoples by driving them to bloodshed and treating forbidden things as lawful.
rows.anchor: Ahmed, Edeb’de Buhârî, Müslim, Beyhakī, Câbir b. Abdillah radıyallâhu anh’tan rivayet eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protection from shuhh does not require a person to be generous in every matter.
rows.anchor: şuhdan korunmak bir kişinin her şeyde cömert olmasına mütevakkıf değildir.

rows.speaker: Mücemmi‘ b. Yahyâ
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says one is free of shuhh by paying zakat, hosting a guest, and helping during a calamity.
rows.anchor: Mücemmi‘[^36] b. Yahyâ’dan merfû‘an rivayet eylemişlerdir ki:

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: Ali says that whoever pays zakat on his wealth is protected from the shuhh of his soul.
rows.anchor: İbn Münzir de Hazret-i Ali radıyallâhu anh’tan şöyle rivayet eylemiştir ki

rows.speaker: Ebû Heyyâc-ı Esedî
rows.claim: Abu Hayyaj al-Asadi reports meeting a man at the Kaaba who only prayed for protection from shuhh, explaining that such protection would keep him from theft, adultery, and wrongdoing; the man was Abdurrahman ibn Awf.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr Taberî, Ebû Heyyâc-ı Esedî’den rivayet eylemiştir

rows.speaker: İbn Zeyd
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says one is protected from shuhh by neither taking what God forbids nor letting it prevent one from fulfilling what God commands; such a person is successful.
rows.anchor: İbn Zeyd de demiştir ki: “Bir kimse Allah’ın nehyettiği bir şey için bir şey almaz
